items.title: From Tutoring Product to Skill Ecosystem: aitutors.me's Multi-Surface Plugin Strategy
items.text: Claude tutors, a public plugin repo, standalone skills, a flashcards import format — how aitutors.me is building surfaces beyond its own subscription product.

items.title: What a Two-Skill Plugin Manifest Reveals About Product Priorities
items.text: A product could ship dozens of skills through its public plugin repo. aitutors.me shipped exactly two. What that restraint actually signals.

items.title: Best AI Flashcard-Authoring Skills and Tools Compared
items.text: Anki add-ons, Quizlet's AI generator, and aitutors.me's flashcards skill compared on what they actually do well — and where each one falls short.

items.title: Six Card Kinds, One QA Gate: What a Good Flashcard Skill Actually Encodes
items.text: Most flashcard tools treat every fact the same way. Looking closely at why one skill refuses to shows what genuinely good study-material design requires.

items.title: The Identity-Anchor Pattern: Keeping an AI Character On-Model at Scale

items.text: aitutors.me ships two skills in one repo — one MIT, one 'do not redistribute.' The contrast is a useful lens on what actually belongs in the open part of a product.

items.title: AI Tutors Flashcards: Turn Any Topic Into Study Cards in Seconds
items.text: A spotlight on the flashcards skill from aitutors.me's plugin repo — an MIT-licensed skill that turns notes into spaced-repetition cards ready to import.

items.title: context-engineering
items.text: Microsoft-native adaptation of context engineering for production-grade agent systems. Bundles the core context and harness engineering skills with Azure and Microsoft Foundry defaults for managed hosted agents, Foundry IQ, Foundry Toolbox, Azure AI Search, Fabric, Entra identity, Responsible AI guardrails, publishing, and memory/state. Ships with a researcher operating system (rubrics, mechanism registry, claim provenance, run state machine, adversarial benchmarks, continuous loop).

items.title: planner
items.text: Planning session that turns an idea or an issue into agent-ready GitHub issues: question rounds, spec, tickets with blocking edges, triage, research and prototypes. The acceptance of a finished spec runs in the controller; /planner:accept points there. Skills load only when invoked.

items.title: dk-ai
items.text: Reusable dk/dk0 skills and agents: analyze dk/dune/noweb projects, build OCaml tools off DkML, create/port dk packages, repair distributions, and convert tests/docs to unified scripts.

items.title: opportunity-finder
items.text: Find hackathons (and later internships/jobs) matched to your resume. Returns title, a short description, and a link only — discovery, never auto-apply.

items.title: simple-explainer
items.text: Explains things in plain language for someone new to them - short sentences, one concrete example or a fenced analogy, jargon named and defined, and a next step they can act on. Covers concepts as well as your own code, errors, and architecture.

items.title: worker
items.text: Worker skills and agents: the issue worker, the reviewer panel, the test hunt and the Claude Code documentation lookup. The ameise controller drives the stages.

items.title: bett3r-routine
items.text: The unattended implementation lane a Blueprint routine runs. The design arrives already agreed as the board's blueprint.md, so the lane is plan → build → verify with no /start or /design: /implement cuts the claude/ work branch, /routine-plan slices blueprint.md, the core /build drives the slices, /routine-verify checks the whole change without opening a PR, and one git trailer tells Blueprint done or needs-human. Requires bett3r-ai-workflow, whose /build, agents, skills and bin it calls.

items.title: steps
items.text: Step the user through a list of open items one at a time, each as its own arrow-key multiple-choice prompt with the recommended option first, acting on each answer before asking the next.

items.title: supervised-build

items.title: v1.110.0-dev.1
items.text:
Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. This release is signed with the key introduced in commit e82a3c6.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.110.0-dev.1

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.110.0-dev.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.110.0-dev.1

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

items.title: Editor publishing updates, Autopilot auto-merge, and more
items.text:
Editor

Choose changes to publish: Each of your changes in the Publish menu has a checkbox, so you can leave some changes out of a publish. The Granular publishing setting is now Show teammates' changes. See Publish specific changes.

Require review before publishing: Admins can turn on Require review before publishing in editor settings so that editors request a review instead of publishing to the deploy branch, and a publisher or admin approves and publishes their changes. You can't turn it on while the deploy branch is protected. See Require review before publishing. Available on Enterprise plans for sites on GitHub.

Dashboard

Support page: Open and track any support cases you have from the Support page. Cases are private by default. You can share a case with your organization. See Track your cases.

Expanded roles: Assign the publisher and commenter roles, compare roles in the permissions table on the Members page, and transfer organization ownership. See Expanded roles. Available on Enterprise plans.

Breaking change

Widget settings removed: You can no longer configure the assistant widget in the dashboard. Widgets you already embed continue working on your authorized sites. To set up the widget on a new site, email support@mintlify.com.

Autopilot

Auto-merge changes: Switch on Auto-merge changes to let Autopilot merge its own pull requests for the kinds of work your team reliably merges. See Auto-merge changes.

GitHub issue events: Ask Autopilot in a chat to run when someone opens, closes as completed, reopens, or labels an issue in a connected GitHub repository. See GitHub repositories.

Translations: Ask Autopilot in a chat to keep your translated pages in sync. It translates merged changes into your site's languages in a separate pull request and checks weekly for missing and outdated translations. See Chat with Autopilot.

Requested work is free: Work you ask Autopilot for directly, in chats on the Autopilot page, Slack, Teams, email replies, or pull request comments, no longer costs credits, even when it opens or updates a pull request. Automated runs, such as those started by a code merge or a schedule, cost 250 credits when they open a pull request, and 250 more each time a later automated run pushes to it. See Credits.

Credit usage: The usage page lists Autopilot as its own category, and each Autopilot usage event links to its session. See Credits.

CLI

mint feedback: Send a bug report, docs issue, or idea to the Mintlify team from your terminal, without signing in.

mint deploy --base: Create a base instead of a docs site. Add --push to push your local clone to the new base.

Default client for mint dev and mint export: mint dev and mint export use a new default client. Pass --classic to use the classic client. See mint export.

Breaking change

Exported archive layout: Archives from mint export store assets in _mintlify/assets/ and no longer include index.txt files. Update your server's caching rules, or export with --classic to keep the previous layout. See Host the export on your own server.

mint validate errors: mint validate fails when a page uses an undefined docs.json variable, an unknown component, or a snippet file that doesn't exist. Fix the findings, or turn off the undefined-variable, unknown-component, or missing-snippet rules with --disable. See mint validate.

AI and MCP

Ranked search: The admin MCP's search tool returns the most relevant pages first with matching snippets, and includes the full content of the top result when it's a confident match. See Content.

Safe page overwrites: Pass the version from read to write_page as baseVersion, and Mintlify refuses the write if the page changed since you read it. See Content.

Inline data: Admin MCP tools replace large base64 images and files with placeholders to keep responses small, and restore the original data when you write the page back. See Inline data.

Navigation location: The admin MCP's read tool returns where a page sits in your navigation, including its parent groups and child pages. See Content.

Invite members: Invite up to 250 people to your organization in one manage_members_sharing call. See Project management.

Review requests: On sites that require review, admin MCP tools request reviews, list and approve review requests, and publish approved changes. See Review requests.

Claude Code and Codex: The MCP page in your dashboard shows the commands to connect the admin MCP from Claude Code and Codex. See Connect to the admin MCP.

Breaking change

Assistant message v1 endpoint: The v1 assistant message endpoint stops working on November 9, 2026. Migrate integrations to the v2 endpoint.

Published sites

Match all changelog tags: Set filterTagMatch: "all" in a changelog page's frontmatter to show only updates that include every selected tag. See Tag filters.

Markdown indexing: Only Markdown served at a .md URL sends a noindex header, so search crawlers that receive Markdown at a page's regular URL can still index the page. See Search indexing.

GraphQL in Markdown: Markdown exports and llms-full.txt include the schema details of GraphQL reference pages, such as an operation's arguments and return type. See API reference pages.

Multi-repository sources: Mintlify merges redirects and applies .mintignore files from every repository source, not only the base source. See Redirects across sources. Available on Enterprise plans.

Azure Repos previews: Create a manual preview for an Azure Repos branch that doesn't have a pull request. See Preview deployments.

Improvements

Desktop app notifications: The desktop app shows a notification for new inbox activity. Click it to open the item in a new tab.

Desktop app windows: Drag a tab out of the tab bar to open it in a new window, or onto another window's tab bar to move it there. The page doesn't reload, so you keep unsaved edits. Right-click selected text in the editor to comment on it.

Comment on snippets: Select text inside a rendered snippet in the editor to comment on it.

Bug fixes

Editor: Wide Mermaid diagrams no longer get clipped. Edits inside HTML elements save, adjacent Steps components stay separate when a page opens, and the cursor lands in the right place after you delete a block. Images embedded in pasted HTML upload as files, copy buttons work in the live preview, and discarding a saved page no longer restores the edit.

Published sites: The version dropdown follows versions with a root-relative href. Clicking blank space around an enlarged image closes it. Screen readers announce heading anchor links by their heading text, and you can reach scrollable code blocks with the keyboard. In the API playground, the request body resets to the selected content type's example, and responses without content don't show an empty media type menu. Sphinx AutoAPI index pages stay out of the Getting Started group. Sites with authentication serve your custom root robots.txt. Switching versions from the version dropdown keeps your place on the page, and preview deployments generate an up-to-date llms-full.txt.

CLI: mint dev no longer gets stuck in a redirect loop when a page path matches a folder of static files. mint deploy --email works without --github, and mint claim explains why it couldn't create a claim link.

Desktop app: Invitations you accept from the desktop app's organization picker take effect.

items.text:
Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. This release is signed with the key introduced in commit e82a3c6.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.1

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.108.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.1

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

items.title: graphify 0.9.103
items.text:
graphify 0.9.103

A broad correctness, performance and robustness release across the extractors, resolution, hooks, the query and update paths, install and the skill runbook.

Extractors

C#: preprocessor directives and #if branches that derail tree-sitter are blanked before parsing (byte-length preserving), so a directive no longer closes a class early and drops later members or calls.

Solidity: library calls (Lib.f(), including aliased imports) and emit/revert/require naming a declared event or error now link to the member they name, gated to a unique visible type and member.

YAML: a << merge sequence gives the earlier anchor precedence for a duplicated key, matching the spec and PyYAML.

Markdown: a code span written as a backslash namespace (\Foo\Bar) or a type-qualified member (Type::member) resolves to the real node; a dotted mention whose method name is a language builtin is no longer dropped.

Python: a bare builtin-named call (raise NotImplementedError(...)) no longer binds to a same-named class in another module unless imported.

Resolution

A call inside a top-level def _main() is attributed to _main, not the public main it collides with after id normalization, without misattributing a class member's type reference.

Hooks

A file unchanged in content is not re-flagged stale by mtime (the extraction hash is checked against the manifest).

A dedicated Grep is held to the strict orientation gate; a Bash file read (cat/head/sed -n) of an in-project code file gets the read nudge; a search whose every target is outside the project emits no project hint; the nudge budget is restored after a Claude Code compaction; and the toplevel anchor keeps working when CDPATH is exported.

Performance

Lower peak memory in load, resolution and extraction; a faster #3252 cross-file repoint; and the watch reconcile pass resolves AST ownership once per file instead of re-reading each header per node — all with identical graph output.

Update / build / cache

graphify update re-extracts only the files whose content changed (identical to a full rebuild); a contended incremental request is recorded instead of dropped. The build write guard no longer counts intentional ghost/dedup folds as drops; cache keys keep their written case.

Query / tree

Source nodes rank above tests and docs (a soft weight) with file-first answers; query reads query_budget/query_depth from .graphifyrc and gains --depth. export tree caps directory children while reporting full totals.

Install / thread-safety

The Pi project skill is written to .pi/skills; uninstall removes the global skill registration it wrote. The ambient scan root is held in a ContextVar so concurrent library callers extracting different roots do not clobber each other.

The AST cache schema is bumped to 39; warm caches re-run the affected extractions.

items.text:
Verify this release

This release candidate is built from f9778e9, the reviewed merge of #50129 into rc/1.107.0. It is published as 1.107.0rc3 on PyPI and v1.107.0-rc.3 on Docker

After the Oct 21 incident (#47826) we replaced the cosign key that signs our Docker images. These images are signed with the new key from commit e82a3c6

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.107.0-rc.3

Why a new 1.107 release candidate

Some users are still running the 1.107 release candidates and needed two GitHub Copilot fixes for per-user credentials. This release brings those fixes to that line. If you are not on a 1.107 release candidate, 1.108.0 is the current stable

What's new in 1.107.0-rc.3

2 PRs. 1 added, 1 fixed. No action needed to upgrade

Changes

Other providers: Added GitHub Copilot per-user credentials on GHE.com tenants with the new optional github_copilot_host field (#47610)

Other providers: Fixed GitHub Copilot per-user connect failing with no Copilot access found when GITHUB_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID is set (#50116)

Backport #50129 · Full changelog

items.title: v1.106.7
items.text:
Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. This release is signed with the key introduced in commit e82a3c6.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.7

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.106.7/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.7

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

items.title: v1.109.0-rc.1
items.text:
Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. This release is signed with the key introduced in commit e82a3c6.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-rc.1

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.109.0-rc.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-rc.1

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

items.title: graphify 0.9.102
items.text:
graphify 0.9.102

A large correctness, performance and workflow release spanning the extractors, the query layer, incremental update, the hooks, the skill runbook and install.

Call-resolution (extractors)

go: same-file member calls resolve through the receiver's type; cross-package pkg.T receivers bind only via the file's import; interface method calls dispatch to implicit implementers (#4966, #4853, #4934).

rust: module-qualified calls (crate::b::helper()) resolve cross-file; calls inside expression-macro arguments are linked (#4944, #4945).

kotlin: overloaded and init {}-block calls resolve; unreachable external-inherited calls are dropped (#4956).

python: a module-level singleton's member calls resolve through its type; a bare method call no longer self-binds (#4972, #4933).

js/ts: class extends through a CommonJS require resolves; a typed tagged template and an import("mod").T<X> annotation no longer half-parse or mint a false dynamic_import edge; default-exported object methods resolve (#4700, #4976, #4967).

solidity: ../ imports resolve to the real file (#4985).

cpp: receiver typing from params/fields, split-header owner binding, local-callable suppression, type-alias exact-spelling (#4946, #4920, #4921, #4951).

Query

Source nodes rank above tests and docs (a soft weight, not exclusion), and answers are file-first (#4982).

graphify query reads query_budget/query_depth from .graphifyrc and gains a --depth flag (#4760).

Incremental update / watch

graphify update re-extracts only the files whose content changed, with a graph identical to a full rebuild; a contended incremental request is recorded instead of dropped (#4800, #4801, #4802).

Build / cache

The write guard no longer counts intentional ghost folds or dedup folds as dropped nodes; independently-sourced semantic evidence survives a fold; cache keys are case-preserving (#4957, #4952, #4927, #4950, #4937).

Hooks

A file unchanged in content is not re-flagged stale by mtime; a dedicated Grep is held to the strict orientation gate; external searches emit no project hint (#4974, #4973, #4979).

Performance

Lower peak memory in load, resolution and extraction, and a faster cross-file repoint — all with identical output (#4960, #4958, #4959, #4981).

Skill / install

The --update runbook re-queues partly-read docs instead of stamping them done; Step 4 threads --force; a hub-bypass report is added; uninstall removes the global skill registration (#4816, #4805, #4704, #4975).

The AST cache schema is bumped to 37; warm caches re-run the affected extractions.

Thanks to @nothariharan, @Deepjyoti-Sarmah, @xiongjianxu, @andrebrait, @ajbmachon, @Shubham-Padkonde, @rohit-jsfreaky, @oleksii-tumanov, @madhusudanpatnaik, @pei711, @Mpasha17, @ayushcodes10, @gitmotion, @briascoi, @madhusudanpatnaik, @AndresDiagoM, @azizur100389, @Ethan-Ethan-Ethan, @jinsoo and @rohit-jsfreaky.

items.title: November 3, 2026
items.text:
Summary

Inboxes can now forward a copy of every email they receive to up to 5 verified addresses. Keep a person in the loop on what your agents receive, or copy mail into an archive or another system, without writing a webhook handler.

What's new?

New endpoints:

POST /v0/forwarding/verifications emails a confirmation code to an address, and POST /v0/forwarding/verifications/confirm verifies it with that code. A verified address can be used anywhere in the organization.

GET, PUT and DELETE on /v0/forwarding, /v0/pods/{pod_id}/forwarding and /v0/inboxes/{inbox_id}/forwarding read, replace and remove the addresses an organization, a pod or an inbox forwards to.

New features:

Nearest level wins: an inbox's list replaces its pod's, and a pod's replaces the organization's. An empty list turns forwarding off at that level.

Verified addresses only: an address receives nothing until whoever reads it confirms the emailed code. unverified on the read lists the addresses still waiting.

Never forwarded: sent mail, spam, bounces, auto-replies, and mail that was already forwarded, so forwards can't loop.

US region only for now: forwarding runs on api.agentmail.to.

Use cases

Build support agents whose incoming mail also reaches a team lead's mailbox.

Copy every email a pod of agents receives into a compliance archive.

Hand incoming mail to a system that already reads email, while the agent keeps working in its inbox.

items.title: graphify 0.9.101
items.text:
graphify 0.9.101

Resolution-accuracy and cache-correctness release across C++, Rust, Python, Go, the build write guard, and incremental rebuilds.

C++

A member call x.m() binds by the receiver's type, now typed from function parameters and class fields and not only locals (void render(Base* b){ b->draw(); } resolves to Base::draw); an untyped or ambiguous receiver keeps its in-file binding (#3215, #4946).

An out-of-line or split-header definition attaches to the unique owner whose class file is in its include set, instead of cross-binding to an unrelated same-named function; ambiguous owners fail closed (#4916, #4920).

A local callable value (a lambda or std::function) is kept out of global call resolution by byte-range binding lifetimes, so it no longer mints a spurious INFERRED call to a same-named global; a later legitimate global call survives (#4917, #4921).

A type-alias reference (using Foo = Bar; then Foo x;) binds by exact spelling and a salted alias keeps its own contains edge (#4951).

Rust

A module-qualified call (crate::b::helper(), super::m::f()) resolves through qualifier-verified cross-file resolution, staying inside the caller's crate (#2135, #4944).

A call written inside an expression macro's arguments (println!("{}", f()), vec![g()]) is linked, gated to an allowlist so macro_rules! bodies and custom DSLs are left alone (#4945).

Python / Go

A bare call inside a method no longer self-binds to a same-named method; it resolves to the imported or module-level function it names (#4933).

Imports resolve across PEP 420 namespace packages split over multiple src/ roots (#4929).

A Go method value reached through a receiver field is linked as an indirect_call (#1566, #4931).

A Go package-level var initialiser references the types it names (#2360, #4932).

Build / cache / rebuild / watch

The write guard no longer refuses a healthy graph when entity dedup folds a saved node into a surviving twin; a genuine loss is still refused (#4940, #4952).

Independently sourced semantic file evidence survives a fold into an AST file-self node; ordinary INFERRED mention ghosts still fold so graphs do not accumulate duplicates (#4896, #4927).

The file-stem alias index only rebinds an edge when the edge's file and the alias target share a language family (#4949).

Cache keys keep their written case so README.md and readme.md no longer collide, and hashed/word-count files are opened through os_long_path (#4925, #4937).

A --code-only graph stays code-only across hook, update and watch rebuilds (#4923, #4939).

A rebuild no longer waits forever when msvcrt.locking is unsupported (#4924, #4926).

A full reconcile evicts source records for an excluded linked git worktree (#4919).

AST-only updates preserve cross-file semantic evidence whose node id collides with a code definition (#4950).

A sliced file is cached only once every slice has succeeded and is assembled in chunk order (#4943, #4947).

The AST cache schema is bumped to 36; warm caches re-run the affected extractions.

Thanks to @nothariharan, @Deepjyoti-Sarmah, @azizur100389, @andrebrait, @ayushcodes10, @madhusudanpatnaik, @Ethan-Ethan-Ethan and @AndresDiagoM.

items.title: graphify 0.9.100
items.text:
0.9.100 (2026-11-01)

Fix: ids a type and a function whose names differ only in case (Foo the class, foo the function) get distinct node ids instead of colliding (which dropped one node and minted a bogus self-loop) (#4904, #4908, thanks @bercedev).

Fix: php a Scope::MEMBER access in a class-level initializer (a const value, a property default, or a parameter/promoted-constructor default) emits a references_constant edge; self::/static::/parent:: are skipped and unknown scopes mint no stub (#4648, #4895, thanks @Jitendarmahara).

Fix: hooks git rev-parse output is decoded as UTF-8, so a linked worktree under a non-ASCII path resolves correctly on Windows instead of mojibake (#4903, thanks @LukeTheoJohnson).

Fix: analyze on a code-only graph the isolated-node question reason says "possible missing edges" rather than referencing documentation gaps that cannot apply (#4887, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

Perf: resolve reference edges are indexed by source once, so JS/TS import resolution no longer re-walks every edge per import (output unchanged) (#4909, #4913, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Docs: skill the skill now says when a graph is worth building, across all generated hosts, while preserving the "if the user invoked /graphify, do it as asked" invariant (#4829, #4906, thanks @TanmayShah29).

Fix: deps the video extra caps PyAV below 19 (av>=11,<19), because PyAV 19 removed the metadata_errors argument that faster-whisper passes unconditionally when opening audio; without the cap a fresh install on Python 3.12+ failed to transcribe (#4842, thanks @SyedFahad7).

Fix: r setClass/setRefClass S4/R5 inheritance declared with contains= now emits an inherits edge (previously only R6Class's inherit= was recognised) (#4902, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: elixir a bare function call resolves to a function in the caller's own module before other modules, instead of binding to the last-walked same-named definition (#4900, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: dart a mixin on A, B clause resolves every superclass constraint, not just the first (#4899, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: fortran a derived type's extends(base) emits an inherits edge, bringing Fortran in line with the other OOP extractors (#4897, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: scala an extension (x: T) def m is scoped to its receiver type T (a method edge to T) instead of leaking to file scope (#2044, #4856, thanks @divakantpandey).

Fix: terraform a node carries its original scope so ids stay stable when a cached project directory is moved, instead of re-deriving the scope from the new path (#4858, #4861, thanks @yUm1k4).

Fix: extract (JVM) Java and Kotlin imports, extends/implements and member calls resolve across files and across the two languages when a written FQN names exactly one sourced type (#4874, #4879, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: export a path/explain/wiki rendering lists every parallel relation between two nodes (via edge_datas), and a raw --no-cluster write marks the graph multigraph so parallel edges survive reload (#4794, thanks @ensell-yes).

Fix: export a partial or failed backup is reported as no backup and retried on the next run, instead of being recorded as a false success (#3769, #4834, thanks @barlowa124).

Fix: affected graphify affected (and query --seed) resolve the same path::Symbol and dotted reference forms explain accepts, reusing explain's resolver, and exit non-zero (3 ambiguous / 4 not-found) on a seed that does not resolve (#4792, #4797, thanks @dupeisen).

Fix: install graphify uninstall removes every platform's user-scope skill (13 were left behind) and the kilo global command; and graphify kilo uninstall removes the kilo skill's references/ sidecar (#4782, #4789, thanks @bercedev).

Feat: llm the Claude backend caches its (stable, large) system prompt with cache_control, counting the cached tokens back into input_tokens, and GRAPHIFY_CLAUDE_PROMPT_CACHE=0 disables it for gateways that reject cache_control (#4835, #4855, #4880, thanks @Jvxoq and @1akashkalita).

Fix: prompt the node-id format description in the extraction prompt matches what ids.py actually produces (word characters kept, non-ASCII letters/digits preserved, ASCII lowercased) instead of the stale "[a-z0-9_] only" wording (#4432, #4799, thanks @dupeisen).

Docs: how-it-works the supported-language count is updated (about 40: 33 tree-sitter grammars plus 7 built-in parsers) and Pass 3 is described as running the configured LLM backend, not Claude only (#4873, thanks @SyedFahad7).

items.title: graphify 0.9.99
items.text:
0.9.99 (2026-10-30)

Feat: path when several routes tie on length, graphify path and the MCP shortest_path tool report the most conservative one: among all shortest paths, the route whose weakest hop is weakest is chosen, and the summary notes it was the weakest of N equal-length routes. Previously an arbitrary equal-length route was returned, so the confidence could overstate how sure the connection is. This is the second half of #4881 (the first half, keeping a collapsed edge's weaker evidence in also_seen, shipped in 0.9.98 via #4891, thanks @SyedFahad7).

Fix: go a call in a package-level var initialiser (including inside a func-literal closure, the common swappable-hook pattern) is credited to the file node instead of being dropped (#2360, #4867, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: go a method value passed as a function argument (Wrap(s.Health)) is linked as an indirect_call, bringing Go to parity with Python/JS for callback-by-method-value; conservatively guarded against field-access false positives (#1566, #4868, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: go a receiver's field whose struct is declared in a sibling file of the same package is typed, so its member calls resolve across the usual struct-here-methods-there Go layout, and the field types persist across incremental rebuilds (#3368, #4866, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: python module.func values listed in a dispatch table ({"a": mod.func_a}, including nested collections) resolve to the referenced functions as indirect_calls instead of being dropped; non-callable, class, and local-receiver values are left alone (#1566, #4773, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: install gemini gets its own global skill dir (~/.gemini/skills/graphify) on Windows instead of colliding with the agents platform's dir; a pre-existing agents skill is noted, not deleted (#2800, #4770, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: install the global OpenCode plugin is written to ~/.config/opencode (co-located with the global skill) instead of the current directory, with install/uninstall/refresh kept symmetric and legacy locations still cleaned up (#3398, #4771, thanks @nothariharan).

Docs: skill the "Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps." instruction is reworded to "unless the fast path above applies," resolving the contradiction with the existing-graph fast path across all generated hosts (#4061, #4721, thanks @nothariharan).

Feat: serve path, explain and neighbors/get_neighbors print an edge's stored confidence_score alongside its tag ([INFERRED 0.75]); EXTRACTED stays bare (1.0 by definition) and a missing or non-finite score keeps the bare tag. Composes with the weakest-hop path summary and the also_seen evidence tags (#4882, #4888, thanks @SyedFahad7).

items.text:
Base

Mintlify Base (beta): A base is a new project type for your team's internal knowledge, such as specs, runbooks, and onboarding guides. Your team and its agents update a base from the editor, the admin MCP, Slack, or Git.

Share base pages to the web: After an admin turns on public links, share a base page with people outside your organization through a public link that also serves a Markdown version for AI tools. See Share a page to the web. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans.

Autopilot

GitLab projects: Autopilot works with repositories on GitLab and uses the GitLab projects you choose as context. See GitLab projects.

Chat in Slack: Mention @mintlify or message the Mintlify app to ask Autopilot questions from Slack. Admins and editors can also change its setup. See Chat in Slack.

Pull request comments: Comment on an Autopilot pull request on GitHub, and Autopilot pushes the requested changes to the same branch and replies in the thread. See Continue a conversation anywhere.

Multi-repository sites: Autopilot works on docs sites built from multiple repositories. Available on Enterprise plans.

CLI

mint migrate: Print step-by-step instructions for migrating content to Mintlify from 21 sources, such as Docusaurus, GitBook, ReadMe, Notion, and PDFs. Pass the --agent flag to have Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Gemini run the migration. See mint migrate.

mint instructions: Coding agents can look up how to do common Mintlify tasks, such as publishing a new site or adding a custom domain, instead of relying on their training data. See mint instructions.

mint agent setup: Install Mintlify skills and connect the admin MCP for Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor with one command. See mint agent setup.

mint validate rules: mint validate checks for content that builds but doesn't render correctly and lists each finding with its file, line, and rule. Repair common issues with --fix, choose rules with --enable and --disable, and get a JSON report with --format json. See mint validate.

Agent signup: A coding agent can create and deploy a site with mint deploy before you have an account, including on every push from GitHub Actions. Claim the site with mint claim. See Agent signup.

Editor

Switch repositories: In a multi-repository project, pick a repository from the menu above your pages to edit its pages, files, and branches. See Edit sources in the web editor. Available on Enterprise plans.

Unpublished changes in the sidebar: Sidebar pages show an Edited or Unpublished badge until you publish them. Projects with auto publish don't show the badges.

Agent branches: Ask the agent to list, create, or switch branches, and it reads, edits, and publishes on the branch it switched to. See Work on other branches.

Components defined in a page: Source mode autocompletes and describes components you define in the page, and jumps to their definitions with F12 or Cmd + click. See Source mode shortcuts.

New pages at the top: The New page button adds pages to the top of your navigation. See Create a page.

Move: The page menu's Move within project option is now Move. See Move a page.

Copy tables: Copy a table as CSV, JSON, Markdown, YAML, XML, or TOON from its block menu.

Auto publish timing: With auto publish on, the editor commits about a minute after you stop editing. See Auto publish.

AI and MCP

Page history: The admin MCP's read_page_history tool lists a page's saved versions and returns the content of any version. See Content.

Pages from uploaded files: Upload a local Markdown file and pass its uploadId to write_page or create_node instead of sending the full page content. See Uploads.

Inbox: The admin MCP's read_inbox tool lists comments, mentions, suggested edits, and invitations to your organization and to pages. See Comments.

Mintlify skill: The admin MCP's read_skill tool reads Mintlify's guide to writing docs, plus your organization's and your own agent skills. See Mintlify skill.

Read-only connections: Send the x-mintlify-toolset: knowledge header to limit an admin MCP connection to search and read tools. See Limit a connection to search and read tools.

Default project: On a connection with access to a single project, read tools no longer need a subdomain. See How editing works.

Projects with auto publish: In projects with auto publish, the admin MCP commits edits to your deploy branch and doesn't create branches. See Projects with auto publish.

Breaking change

Admin MCP upload tools renamed: upload_image is now upload_file, and finalize_image_upload is now finalize_file_upload. Update prompts or scripts that call the old names. See Uploads.

Published sites

Emails authentication: Invite readers outside your organization by email, and Mintlify hosts their sign-in with a password or a one-time code. See Emails authentication. Contact sales to turn it on for your site.

Full-page search results: Turn on Full-page search results in your Site settings to give readers a search results page at /search that they can bookmark and share. See Full-page search results.

Navigate from custom scripts: Call window.mintlify.navigate to send readers to another page without a full reload. See Navigate to another page.

Markdown export: In .md pages, cards, accordions, and tabs render as blockquotes that open with [card], [accordion], or [tab], so AI tools can tell them apart. Props written as JSX, such as a Tooltip's tip, render as Markdown. See Components.

Go SDK references: Go packages that mix kinds group their pages under Interfaces, Structs, Types, and Functions. Pass -exclude-symbols to the extractor to leave symbols out. See Generated pages.

TypeDoc overview pages: TypeDoc artifacts with a README get an overview page that indexes the library's symbols. See Generated pages.

Improvements

Desktop app tabs: Tabs signed in to different organizations work side by side. In the editor, Cmd + click a link to one of your pages to open that page in a new tab, or right-click it to open it in a new tab or window.

Thumbs-only feedback: The feedback export API includes thumbs up and thumbs down votes submitted without a comment. See Get feedback.

Site settings: The project General settings page is now called Site.

Previews when you turn on authentication: Turning on authentication through the API or admin MCP deletes previews that don't have authentication, matching the dashboard. To keep them, pass previewDeployments: "keep".

Deleted subdomains: After you delete a project, Mintlify reserves its subdomain for your organization for 30 days. See Delete a project.

Bug fixes

Editor: Code blocks you type with three backticks in a list item stay in that list item. Cards render inside custom components in visual mode, table cell selections stay after you drag, and custom component previews load your fonts and repository CSS. Character references and hidden export blocks survive saves and deletions. Parent page titles show in the sidebar after you refresh. The editor keeps syncing when browser storage stops accepting writes, and Cmd + J toggles the agent while you type in it.

Published sites: Static files load on sites with authentication on custom domains. RSS feeds work on sites with authentication. Go references no longer repeat description sentences and render GitHub alerts as callouts. Sphinx references keep their module navigation and type links.

CLI: mint validate no longer crashes during connectivity checks. mint dev picks up snippet edits you made while it was stopped. MDX parse errors suggest escaping <.

Dashboard: The sign-in page explains when your organization requires SSO.

Desktop app: Session refreshes no longer clear stored data or reload your tabs.

items.title: graphify 0.9.98
items.text:
0.9.98 (2026-10-30)

Fix: build when duplicate same-relation edges collapse, the losing (weaker-confidence) copy's provenance is kept in an also_seen list on the surviving edge instead of being discarded, so the weaker evidence is not silently lost; the field is serialized to graph.json and is idempotent across rebuilds (#4881, #4891, thanks @SyedFahad7).

Fix: csharp a C# method node is labelled with its owning type (MyClass.Method) instead of a bare Method, so same-named methods across types are distinguishable; node ids and edges are unchanged (display label only) (#4883, #4889, thanks @SyedFahad7).

Feat: path graphify path and the MCP shortest-path output report the overall path confidence as the weakest hop (lowest confidence tier, then lowest score), with a summary line naming that hop (#4885, #4892, thanks @SyedFahad7).

Fix: path an endpoint written Type.Member resolves to the member node, not the containing type, so graphify path "Exporter.Run" "PdfReport.Build" finds the real call route; exact names and file names still win first, and a Type.Member whose member does not exist fails closed (#4884, #4893, thanks @SyedFahad7).

Fix: extract file ids and per-declaration ids are kept distinct, so a top-level declaration whose name matches its file (for example class Js in a.js) is no longer silently dropped on an id collision; cross-file references bind to the declared id (#4854, #4857, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: dedup when a cross-file document mention and an AST node collide on a defining id, the AST node keeps the id instead of being dropped, while same-file enrichment, extension twins and single-definer cases are left as-is (#4859, #4872, thanks @TanmayShah29; duplicate approach in #4871 by @ayushcodes10).

Fix: build a two-file import cycle (a imports b, b imports a) is reported in the default undirected build, and the stamp is cleared correctly on incremental/watch rebuilds so a dropped import no longer leaves a stale cycle (#4839, #4841, thanks @Mpasha17; duplicate approach in #4852 by @legendteddy).

Fix: extract a relative JS/TS import carrying a ?query or #fragment suffix (./mod.js?v=1) resolves to the real module instead of a phantom node; Node #subpath imports are left untouched (#4860, #4876, thanks @Jitendarmahara; duplicate approach in #4869 by @mirzasnowy).

Fix: go a receiver bound with var x = T{} or var x = &T{} (a composite literal) is typed as T, matching the x := T{} form, so its member calls resolve (#4843, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: verilog a SystemVerilog class constructor (function new(...), which has no return type) gets its own node, method edge and parameter-type references (#4848, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: powershell using module/using assembly drops a real file extension (Helpers.psm1 to helpers) but keeps a dotted module name with no extension intact (Az.Accounts) (#4847, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: solidity a free-function using {a, b} for T set emits uses edges for each named function, not just the single-library using Lib for T form (#4846, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: commonlisp a defclass whose superclass is defined later in the same file binds to that local node instead of minting a sourceless stub (#4845, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: pascal inherited and inline form component blocks (.lfm/.dfm) are recognised, so a later object block keeps its correct parent instead of being re-parented by a corrupted nesting stack (#4844, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: serve when two nodes tie in a lookup and differ only by case, the one spelled exactly as queried wins (the others stay reachable one tier down) instead of every spelling being refused as ambiguous (#4870, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: export the Cypher text export keys MERGE on the stable node id and sets the label separately, so re-importing after a label change updates the node instead of creating a duplicate (#4878, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

Fix: pdf the converted-text cache is keyed on the resolved source path, so two PDFs with the same relative name in different roots do not poison each other within one process (#4851, thanks @xunguangzlj-cloud).

items.title: v1.109.0-dev.2
items.text:
Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. This release is signed with the key introduced in commit e82a3c6.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-dev.2

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.109.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-dev.2

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

items.title: October 28, 2026
items.text:
Summary

Inboxes can now carry a signature that AgentMail adds to every message they send. Your agents no longer have to remember to append contact details or branding, and every message from the inbox looks the same whether it was sent through the API, the MCP server, or SMTP.

What's new?

signature on create and update: an object with text and an optional html. Send null on update to remove it.

Every send path: sends, replies, reply-alls, forwards, and drafts, including scheduled ones, get the signature right after your content and above any quoted or forwarded message.

No duplicates: a message whose body already contains the signature is sent as written.

Returned on the inbox:signature appears on inbox responses when one is set.

Use cases

Build support agents whose replies always end with the team's name, hours, and help-center link.

Give sales agents a consistent signature with a logo linked by URL, without changing agent prompts.

Update one inbox setting to change the signature on every agent that sends from it.

items.title: graphify 0.9.97
items.text:
0.9.97 (2026-10-27)

Security: rationale redaction credential redaction for rationale labels moves to a single pre-cache choke point (_redact_rationale_labels inside _safe_extract), so no extractor can skip it, and it now covers more leak shapes: URL userinfo with an empty user or with //@ in the password, PEM private-key bodies, tokens glued to surrounding text by _ (for example ghp_...), Slack xoxe- refresh tokens, short JWTs, and Common Lisp docstrings that previously built labels without redacting. Benign strings (hashes, sk- prose, URLs without userinfo) are left alone (#4647, thanks @0xkaushik-ai).

Security: deps anyio is floored to >=4.14.2 in the mcp extra, above CVE-2026-63374 (an IDNA 2003 vs 2008 hostname-validation bypass that let a MITM on a non-ASCII domain present a cert for a different ASCII host, CVSS 9.3). anyio is only a transitive dependency and the lockfile already resolves 4.15.1, so this is a floor to stop a future re-resolution from regressing.

Fix: markdown ATX headings parse per CommonMark: a trailing run of # is not part of the heading text (## Setup ## is "Setup"), up to three spaces of indent are allowed (four is an indented code block), and a hash-only line like ## ## mints no node (#4790, #4791, thanks @jaimemartinez).

Fix: markdown fenced code blocks are tracked by CommonMark rules (backtick and tilde fences, info strings, matching close length), so a line that looks like a heading inside a fence no longer leaks as structure, and a heading after a ~~~ block that contains a ``` line is no longer lost (#4787, #4788, thanks @jaimemartinez).

Fix: yaml structural extraction reads the composed node tree, so keys carry their written spelling and their own source line instead of all landing on line 1, and YAML 1.1 bare keys like on/off/yes/no are no longer folded to booleans (a workflow on: block is extracted, not turned into a True node) (#4784, #4785, thanks @jaimemartinez).

Fix: razor a component's @implements interfaces are extracted as implements edges instead of being silently dropped (#4820, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: terraform an aliased provider block gets its own alias-qualified node (so two provider "aws" blocks no longer collapse into one and lose attributes), and a provider = aws.west reference resolves to it instead of dangling; a local literally named provider is no longer misread (#4819, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: cobol paragraphs that follow a nested END PROGRAM reattach to the enclosing program instead of sticking to the nested one, via a program stack (#4824, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: blade a wire:click directive binds the bare method name: dotted modifiers (wire:click.prevent="submit") are matched, call arguments are trimmed from the name (deleteItem(5) binds deleteItem), and a $-prefixed magic action mints no fabricated edge (#4823, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: pascal a record is recognised as a type with its own methods in the regex fallback (the default path without the optional pascal extra), matching the tree-sitter path; operator members are extracted too (#4825, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: vbnet an Operator declaration is extracted as an operator-kind member of its class and its body is walked for calls, so a helper call inside an operator no longer vanishes (#4821, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: fortran a call resolves to the subroutine it actually names instead of a target salted with the calling file's name (which never resolved), using the extractor's own cross-file stub idiom (#4795, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: cli graphify query --help/-h (and now graphify explain --help/-h) with nothing else prints usage instead of running a literal query for the text "--help"; a longer question that merely contains "--help" as a substring still runs as a query (#4830, thanks @curl-man).

Fix: js a nested (inner) function no longer leaks into the file-wide name map, so a call elsewhere in the file binds to the top-level function of that name rather than an inner one it cannot see; recursion, shadowing and sibling scopes resolve correctly (ports the Python scope scheme to JS/TS) (#4767, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: ocaml every binding in an and-chained module ... and ... or class ... and ... is extracted, not just the first, so later bindings are no longer silently dropped; each carries its own source line (#4822, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: verilog a SystemVerilog class task method is modeled like a function one (its own node, method edge and parameter-type references), and a task-local variable no longer leaks as a false field reference on the class (#4774, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: build an edge with no relation is dropped instead of persisted, on both the build and the raw --no-cluster write paths, and alias folding (relationship to relation) runs before the check (#4810, thanks @legendteddy; reproducer also filed as #4826 by @sunhouy).

Fix: build the shrink guard counts a saved document-mention node that folds into its AST file twin on reload as present, not lost, so a cluster-only write is no longer refused when nothing was actually lost (#4778, #4779, thanks @AndresDiagoM).

Fix: detect a linked git worktree whose main checkout resolves inside the scan root is pruned, so a sibling worktree no longer gets indexed as a second full copy of the repo (#4683, #4833, thanks @barlowa124; duplicate work in #4685 by @AndresDiagoM).

Fix: resolution an inline comment in a pnpm-workspace glob is stripped per YAML rules, and a glob that Path.glob rejects (a ** component or an absolute pattern) is skipped with a warning instead of crashing the whole extract run (#4681, #4687, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: report a community hub [[wikilink]] is slugged through the same export._obsidian_safe_stem the export uses, so the link matches the file the export actually writes instead of dangling (#4696, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: wiki a community relabelled only by letter case keeps its article instead of having the sweep delete the file the run just wrote; on a case-sensitive filesystem the stale lower-case twin is unlinked rather than renamed over the fresh file (which would silently restore the old body) (#4508, #4798, thanks @dupeisen).

Fix: query filler verbs get/gets/got/getting are dropped from query terms (like the existing work/works), so a framework hub labelled "Get" is not pulled in as a BFS seed by an exact-match bonus; node lookups for a literal Get still resolve (#4686, thanks @AndresDiagoM).

items.title: October 27, 2026
items.text:
Summary

Calendar invitations your agent builds itself and sends from an inbox now go on that inbox's calendar. Attendees' replies are tracked on the event, the same as for invitations sent with the Calendar API.

What's new?

Your own .ics invitations land on your calendar: an invitation the inbox sends as an attachment, with METHOD:REQUEST and the inbox as ORGANIZER, becomes an event with source: api. The sent email gets calendar_event_id, and a calendar.event.created webhook is sent. AgentMail emails nobody, because your email already went out.

Replies apply: attendees' accept, decline and tentative replies update the event and send calendar.event.responded, where before they were ignored.

Your later emails sync it: a newer REQUEST updates the event, and a CANCEL cancels it or removes the attendees it names.

Move to the API whenever you like:PATCH the event with send_invites: true and attendees get the update under your original UID.

Limits: up to 100 new imported events per inbox and 200 per organization each day. PUBLISH files, replies, single-date changes and invitations organized by someone else are not imported.

items.title: graphify 0.9.96
items.text:
0.9.96 (2026-10-25)

Security: deps the Pillow floor is raised to >=13.0.0 on Python 3.11+ (staying at >=12.3.0 on 3.10, which Pillow 13 no longer supports) and pypdf to >=6.19.0, and the lockfile is refreshed to patched versions of transitive dependencies (pyjwt, cryptography, certifi, urllib3, anyio, fsspec, soupsieve, virtualenv). This clears the bulk of the open Dependabot advisories; the Pillow image-parsing CVEs are only patched upstream for Python 3.11+, so a 3.10 install keeps the newest 3.10-compatible Pillow.

Fix: llm a chunk that failed before returning a response no longer has its files reported as model omissions; the warning distinguishes a failed chunk from a genuine omission, and both are still re-dispatched (#3616, #4752, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @GREYGROUPJP).

Fix: watch a Markdown file that detect() classifies as a paper (arXiv markers, an Abstract) is included in the watch quick-scan rebuild instead of contributing zero nodes; a paper that already has a semantic layer is still excluded from the AST quick-scan (#4750, #4751, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @yeochul-jeon).

Fix: prs every unfinished CheckRun status (WAITING, REQUESTED, PENDING, ...) counts as pending CI, so a PR gated on a deployment-protection job is no longer read as ready (#4730, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: export an Obsidian note lists every parallel relation between two nodes (for example both imports and calls) instead of only the first edge (#4731, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: build a hyperedge whose members are given under the members/node_ids aliases has its numeric member ids coerced to strings like the canonical nodes list, so the hyperedge is no longer dropped (#4732, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: llm a code node whose confidence is written in a different case (extracted/Extracted) is still evidence-checked before it folds to the EXTRACTED enum, so an un-verified node is not presented as solid (#4733, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: python a member call binds to the method it actually spells rather than a case/underscore-folded twin (run() no longer resolves to _run()); a lone folded method still resolves, and a genuine collision fails closed (#4734, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: zig a call no longer crosses between a method and a same-named free function; a bare call binds the free function and a receiver call binds the method (#4755, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: dart an unnamed extension on T { } declaration is detected and extracted (the name is optional), so its members attach to the extended type (#4741, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: llm the DeepSeek backend sends its output cap as max_tokens (which DeepSeek honours) rather than max_completion_tokens (which it ignores), so responses are no longer silently uncapped (#4739, #4753, thanks @Ethereal49; reported by @snapp-kenya).

Fix: extract XAML codebehind (*.xaml to *.xaml.cs) resolves deterministically regardless of directory iteration order, so a graph built on a case-sensitive filesystem is stable (#4747, thanks @anishraja04).

Fix: extract the AST cache hit rate is reported over the file total, not the uncached set, so a warm run no longer prints a misleading "100% uncached" line (#4740, #4746, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @lavaxun).

Fix: dedup a node id legitimately shared by two files as a module/namespace no longer prints a spurious "minted by two different files" warning (#4756, thanks @idachev).

Fix: python the member-call resolver binds only Python callers to Python targets, so a same-named class in another language is no longer mis-bound as a call (#4757, thanks @idachev).

Fix: cli the PreToolUse hook reminders are worded as facts rather than imperatives, so the agent's tool-result stream no longer reads them as prompt injection and ignores them (#2202, #4764, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: llm the Ollama context window is sized from an estimate that counts non-Latin characters as whole tokens and from the real system-prompt length, so a non-English or long prompt is no longer silently truncated (#4414, #4761, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: cli graphify extract records each run's token usage to graphify-out/cost.json (the same ledger the skill writes), so a standalone extract refresh updates the cost history (#1769, #4765, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: ts chained TypeScript decorators (@(Link().toMany())) are recovered as a decorator reference, and a lossy-parse warning names the real error region (#4711, #4715, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: js a const X = require('pkg') binding for an external package keeps its node (with the package as source) so new X() still resolves, while a require of a corpus-local file still folds to the required module (#4688, #4702, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: detect generated MSBuild obj/ and bin/ output is pruned only when build evidence is present (restore/runtime markers nearby), so a C# project scanned after a build no longer ingests generated sources while a real src/bin stays (#4742, thanks @Great-Peace).

Fix: watch each watch rebuild is bounded by GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT (default 600s, 0 disables), with a thread-Timer fallback where SIGALRM is unavailable or watch() runs off the main thread (a SIGALRM arm there raises ValueError and would tear the watcher down before the rebuild ran), so a hung rebuild no longer stalls the watcher (#2173, #4724, thanks @danieldutu).

Fix: robot each duplicate test-case name gets its own node (salted by line), so two tests with the same name are kept distinct (#4697, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: vbnet external namespaces and types emit a sourceless stub carrying an empty source_file sentinel like other languages, instead of a node that fails validation (#4725, #4728, thanks @madanlalit; reported by @alopezradicle).

Fix: rust a use is scoped to the crate it names, so use serde_json::Value no longer resolves to a same-named type in another crate; a named pub use re-export is followed and a manifest-less binding stays INFERRED (#4699, #4712, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: python a call through a field injected from a constructor parameter, or through a local typed by a method's return annotation, resolves to the target method (INFERRED); it requires a single unambiguous producer and class (#4726, thanks @keny11300).

Fix: dedup an LLM-marked cross-document reference stub that collides with its real definition is namespaced instead of silently dropped, so neither node is lost (#4738, #4743, thanks @SinghAman21; reported by @snapp-kenya).

Perf: update a graphify update with no relevant input change skips the detect/extract/build pipeline and leaves the outputs untouched, keyed on the scan file-set, config, .graphifyrc, extractor epoch, and an output-completeness stamp; a scanned file with no manifest row (including one whose extraction previously failed) still forces a full rebuild so a later fix is never skipped (#4740, #4748, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @lavaxun).

v4.1.4: Token Gesture

Generated CLIs now preserve remote transports, empty arrays, and parameters whose names collide with their own helpers; mounted servers honor session visibility and mounted_components_raise_on_load_error, a stale client context no longer closes a newer session, and OAuth provider wrappers accept identity assertions. items.title: October 24, 2026
items.text:
Summary

message.received for an email with a calendar invitation now arrives with calendar_event_id already set, so your agent can answer the invitation straight from the webhook instead of fetching the message again.

What's new?

Invitation emails wait for their event: for an email with a calendar attachment, message.received (webhook and WebSocket) waits until the invitation has been added to the inbox's calendar, at most 20 seconds, and the message carries calendar_event_id.

Other email is unchanged: only emails with a calendar attachment wait, typically a second or two.

No calendar_event_id means the invitation wasn't added: a reply or cancellation for an event the calendar doesn't have, a sender that couldn't be verified as the organizer, or a slow import. Get the message again later to check.

items.title: Autopilot, dashboard inbox, editor agent skills, and more
items.text:
Autopilot

Autopilot (beta): Autopilot is a proactive agent that opens pull requests to keep your documentation up-to-date, and performs ongoing maintenance such as a daily quality check. Turn it on from the Autopilot page in your dashboard. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans.

Review suggestions: Autopilot's pull requests appear under Suggestions, where you can preview, accept, close, or ask for changes in a chat. See Review suggestions.

Feature launches: For a large launch, Autopilot tracks the feature and keeps a draft pull request current until the code merges. See Feature launches.

Integration events: Ask Autopilot in a chat to run when an event happens in a connected shared integration, such as a new Linear issue. See Slack and other integrations.

Signed commits: GitHub signs Autopilot's commits and shows them as Verified, so they work with branch protection rules that require signed commits. See How Autopilot opens pull requests.

Editor and dashboard

Agent skills: Add reusable instructions that the agent loads when a request matches them. Create skills, upload SKILL.md files, .skill or .zip archives, or folders, or ask the agent to save a skill while you chat. Admins can move personal skills to your organization.

Inbox: The inbox collects replies, mentions in comments and page content, comments on pages you own, and shared private pages. Filter by section and date range, and mark everything as read at once.

Edits from comment threads: Ask @mintlify in a comment to change a page and the agent performs edits then updates the comment thread. See Ask the Mintlify agent.

Show all branches: Choose whether the branch menu lists every branch in your repository. See Show all branches.

Commit co-authors: Credit teammates as co-authors on editor commits. See Editor settings.

Delete agent chats: Delete chats from the agent's session history.

Source mode: Fold component blocks and code fences and keep your scroll position when you switch between visual and source mode. JSX attribute expressions highlight as JavaScript, and style objects autocomplete CSS properties and describe them on hover.

Mermaid diagrams: Visual mode hides Mermaid code by default and remembers whether you show it.

Inline SVG and custom pages: Visual mode draws inline <svg> blocks. On pages in custom or frame mode, components respond to clicks and you can select and copy text.

Page titles in URLs: Editor URLs and copied page links include the page title, such as /~/Getting-Started-<id>. Existing links still work.

Copy and move pages: The page menu's Copy to… and Move to… options are now Copy to a project and Move within project. After you copy a page to another project, the editor opens the copy. See Copy a page to another project.

Billing page: Set overages and spend limits for each project and compare plans on the redesigned Billing page. On Pro and Enterprise plans, reserve credits for a project. See Overages.

Automations in project settings: Automations moved to your project settings.

Desktop app

Copy tab links: Right-click a tab and select Copy Link to copy the link to its page.

What's new: See recent changes to the desktop app in its settings.

Published sites

Page styles: Add a <style> block to a page to style only that page's content. See Custom CSS.

Styling hooks: Style the search bar, search dialog, and theme layout with stable data-search-item and data-layout-item attributes. Log in and log out links in the sidebar have the login-link and logout-link classes, like the links in the navigation bar. See Class and element hooks.

JSON request bodies: Switch between Form and JSON to edit request bodies in the API playground. See Edit request bodies as JSON.

Optional API fields: Set api.optional to collapse, expand, or always show optional fields in the API playground. See API settings.

Markdown export: .md pages render components, Visibility content, and snippets as plain Markdown, and keep the text of components such as Frame, Tile, and Prompt. Links to pages in your navigation point to their .md versions, and on most sites internal links use your site's full URL. See Components and HTML.

Go SDK references: Generate SDK reference pages for Go packages with the go format and mintlify-go-extractor. See Go.

Javadoc navigation: SDK reference navigation for Javadoc artifacts groups symbols by kind within each package. See Generated pages.

Classic thumbnails: Generated OG images use the classic layout by default. Thumbnails with a custom background image and no preset keep their original layout. See thumbnails.

Google Fonts from your domain: On sites without authentication, Mintlify serves Google Fonts from your docs domain, so readers' browsers don't connect to Google.

Assistant widget text size: Set appearance.fontSize to a number from 12 to 20 to change the text size of the assistant widget in pixels.

Preview access through the API: Pass auth to the Trigger preview deployment endpoint to protect a preview with a password or dashboard login.

Old previews: If you change your repository, Mintlify deletes previews from the previous repository after seven days. See Preview lifetime.

CLI

Generate docs.json files: mint dev generates a docs.json file from your folder structure when your directory doesn't have one. See Local preview.

Preview on other devices: mint dev listens only on localhost. To open the preview on a phone or another computer, run mint dev --host. See Preview on other devices.

Breaking change

mint test removed: The CLI no longer includes the mint test command. Remove it from scripts and CI workflows that call it.

AI and MCP

Admin MCP editing: edit_page applies up to 100 replacements in one call, create_node writes into a page that already exists at the path, and write_page and edit_page report markup the editor drops. See Content.

Admin MCP navigation: list_nodes returns fewer fields for each node and leaves out uploaded files unless you filter for them. Update scripts that read other fields. list_deployments returns each project's projectType. See Navigation.

Admin MCP deploy status: deployment_status reports whether published changes are live, and suggest_edit accepts a comment that explains the change. See Branches and publishing.

Bring your own model: Starter questions and the commit messages and pull request details for editor publishes also run on your key. See Bring your own model. Available on Enterprise plans.

API request examples: When readers ask the assistant how to call an API, its answers include a minimal request example based on your docs.

Assistant API limits: The assistant API no longer has a per-IP daily request limit. See Create assistant message.

Conversation IDs: Assistant conversation exports include a conversationId that groups turns from the same conversation. See Assistant conversations.

Bug fixes

Editor: Imported .md files parse as Markdown, and Notion Markdown exports are cleaned up on import. HTML links to sections on the same page scroll in visual mode. Bold and italic formatting stays after you post a comment. New branches no longer reuse names of deleted branches. Interrupted agent responses reconnect. OpenAPI page descriptions render components. Typing --- in source mode starts frontmatter. Template literals inside HTML no longer gain indentation when you save, and inline HTML tables keep their layout when you click a cell.

Published sites: Switching versions keeps you on the same page when the other version files it elsewhere. Price-like dollar amounts render as text instead of math. Scrolling in Safari continues over horizontal scrollbars. MCP discovery documents use your custom domain. On sites with authentication, the contextual menu's MCP options point to the authenticated MCP server. RSS items keep their original dates. Tailwind classes passed through variables and expressions get their styles.

API playground: Request examples use server variable defaults when the playground is hidden. Requests without a body sent through the playground proxy no longer fail with 415 errors.

Previews: View Preview links open the preview's home page when the linked page isn't in the build. Leftover previews from a previous repository no longer block new previews.

Offline exports: API playground icons load from the export.

Desktop app: Switching organizations no longer reloads every tab. Tabs show the editor branch, and new tabs keep your theme.

Dashboard: Visit page stays disabled until your site's first build is live. Pending custom domains appear in your custom domain settings. Choosing no spend limit no longer turns off overages. Projects you delete leave the project list right away, and a new project that reuses a deleted project's subdomain starts with an empty editor.

Automations: Scheduled Update from code changes runs no longer skip commits that are pushed after their commit date.

items.title: v2.11.0
items.text:
Custom landing pages

Minor release adding a customizable page at the MCP URL with landing.tsx, plus agent streaming, OAuth client, and CLI fixes.

New (server, @mcp-use/cli): a landing.tsx in the MCP root replaces the page a browser sees at the MCP URL. mcp-use dev and mcp-use build find it (also under --mcp-dir) and mcp-use start serves the built page. It renders on the server and hydrates in the browser; without it, the built-in page is served as before (#2648)

New (server): mcp-use/landing exports React-free hooks for the page: useServerInfo(), useToolList(), usePromptList(), useResourceList() and useInstallTargets(). Server info always ships to the page; each list ships only when the page's import graph uses its hook (#2648)

New (server): getInstallTargets({ url, name }) returns install links and commands for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, VS Code Insiders, ChatGPT and the Manufact Inspector, for use outside the server such as on a docs site (#2648)

New (server): landing.tsx can export const metadata (title, description, icon, image) to set the page title, meta description, and Open Graph and Twitter tags (#2648)

New (@mcp-use/cli): Tailwind classes work in landing.tsx without a CSS file and CSS imports are bundled. In dev, edits use Fast Refresh, adding or deleting landing.tsx switches pages live, and a broken edit keeps serving the last working page. Builds honor MCP_ASSETS_URL (#2648)

New (create-mcp-use-app): every template includes a Tailwind-styled landing.tsx; blank and mcp-server add React and its types, and every template's tsconfig.json typechecks landing.tsx (#2648)

Fix (server, @mcp-use/cli): landing pages set data-theme from the OS color scheme before first paint so dark: classes work; a page whose CSS imports Tailwind itself owns Tailwind; and in mcp-use dev the page's stylesheets load before hydration (#2880)

Update (server): ChatGPT install steps follow the Plugins flow (Plugins → Add → Add Custom MCP Server) instead of developer mode and the Connectors tab (#2648)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use start --with-inspector serves the Inspector at /inspector when basePath is "/", and mcp-use dev prints /inspector instead of //inspector (#2555)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use client and mcp-use screenshot install a matching @mcp-use/client when they auto-install it, including on Windows where the install always failed (#2853)

Fix (@mcp-use/agent): the OpenAI Responses provider emits tool-call argument events, so MCPAgent.stream() and streamEvents() report steps for tool calls on OpenAI models (#2551)

Fix (@mcp-use/agent): MCPAgent.stream() returns and saves to memory only the final turn's text, the same as run(), instead of gluing on text written before tool calls (#2723)

Fix (@mcp-use/agent): RemoteAgent.run no longer rejects successful responses whose body has no error field, and error messages show the error instead of [object Object] (#2651)
