items.title: API reference pages in the editor, Admin MCP improvements, and more
items.text:
Breaking changes

Mintlify Index discontinued: The Index API returns 410 Gone and the Index MCP server tells connected agents to remove it. The dashboard no longer shows Index API keys, and the CLI no longer includes the mint index command.

Admin MCP tool changes: The admin MCP renames save to publish. Tools that edit content require a branch argument, and create_branch, discard, and status replace checkout, discard_session, and get_session_state. Dedicated project management tools replace the search_code_operations and execute_code code mode tools. Update prompts or scripts that call the old tools.

OpenAPI and API playground

OpenAPI 3.2: Mintlify accepts OpenAPI 3.2 documents. Tag hierarchies become nested navigation groups, and the API playground supports 3.2 additions such as the QUERY method and whole query string parameters. To upgrade a 3.1 document, change its openapi version.

Streaming responses: The API playground shows streaming responses as they arrive. Click Stop to end the request.

Editor and dashboard

API reference pages in the editor: Pages with openapi or api frontmatter show their endpoint and generated fields in the editor, so you can edit the content around them. See Pages.

Section links: Links to /page#heading open the page at that heading. Copy link to section in the block actions menu copies a dashboard link to the heading, and pasted section links show the section name.

Thumbnail settings: Set thumbnail overrides in page settings and in the settings for groups, tabs, and other navigation sections. See Edit page settings.

Unpublished site configuration: The site configuration view lists the sections with unpublished changes in a banner and marks them in the sidebar.

Print a page: Press Cmd + P to print the page content without the editor interface. See Keyboard shortcuts.

Agent mentions: Ask the agent to add teammate and page mentions to your content.

Haiku 5.5: Choose Haiku 5.5 in the agent's model picker.

Publishes: The Activity section of the dashboard is now Publishes, with Overview and Previews pages. See Deployments.

Admin MCP in the sidebar: Admin MCP settings and credentials have their own MCP item in the dashboard sidebar. Search MCP client credentials moved to the Docs MCP section of your project settings.

Regional translation targets: The Translate content automation can translate into British, Australian, and Canadian English and into Mexican and Latin American Spanish. See Manage automations.

Published sites

OG image presets: Choose a classic, headline, or minimal layout for generated OG images, with custom fonts, a brand or neutral background, and an eyebrow label above the title. Override the settings for individual pages and sections. See thumbnails.

Preview OG images: Run mint og to render a page's OG image to a PNG file.

Visibility by sign-in state and group: Show content only to signed-in readers, signed-out readers, or specific groups, and hide it from groups with excludes. See Visibility.

Regional language variants: navigation.languages accepts regional codes such as en-GB, es-MX, and es-419, and the language switcher shows the region. Language routing sends visitors to the variant that matches their browser. See Regional variants.

hreflang tags: Sites with multiple languages link each page to its translations with hreflang tags, so search engines can show readers the right language. See Alternate language links.

TypeDoc categories: SDK reference navigation follows the @category and @group tags in your TypeDoc artifact. See Generated pages.

Preview deployments: The robots.txt file on preview deployments disallows crawling.

Navigation on authenticated sites: Signed-out visitors on sites with authentication see the public navigation on first load, without layout shifts.

Server-rendered custom components: Custom components that you define with export and that only place their props into HTML render on the server, so they no longer pop in after the page loads. See React components.

AI and MCP

Admin MCP comment tools: The admin MCP can read comment threads, start a comment, suggest a tracked change, reply, and resolve threads. See Comments.

Merge from the admin MCP: Pass merge: true to publish to merge the branch's pull request when your project allows edits to the deploy branch. See Branches and publishing.

User ID on MCP events: Search tool calls through an authenticated MCP server record the signed-in user's sub claim as user_id in analytics streaming. Available on Enterprise plans.

Redacted assistant conversations: Email addresses and phone numbers in assistant conversations appear redacted in the dashboard, CSV exports, and the analytics API. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans.

Bug fixes

Editor: Footnotes render instead of showing a warning. Keyboard text selection works across tables. Comment cards stay anchored when you switch tabs, and block menu actions follow their block when content shifts. Autolinked URLs include their paths, queries, and sections and leave out trailing punctuation. Bare domains link to https://. The docs.json tab is titled Site settings.

Comments: The comment popover hides reply and actions when you can't comment. If your organization uses roles, admins can delete any comment or thread.

Published sites: Tabs no longer clip ordered list numbers from 10 up. Related pages pick the right language for index pages.

CLI: mint a11y checks files that use custom heading IDs. mint broken-links reports every page it can't parse instead of stopping at the first, no longer flags valid code inside <MDX> fragments, and resolves relative links in snippets.

Desktop app: Switching organizations no longer switches you back to the previous organization.

Multi-repo: Each GitHub source fetches content through its own installation.

Analytics API: Export date parameters accept ISO 8601 time zone offsets and fractional seconds.

items.text:
OAuth Proxy for non-DCR providers

Canary release (mcp-use@2.10.0-canary.4) adding an OAuth authorization server in front of identity providers without dynamic client registration, secret-free production builds, and .gitignore-aware deployments. Stable v2.10.0 has not shipped.

New (server): oauthProxy() in mcp-use/oauth makes the MCP server its own authorization server in front of GitHub (github()), Google (google()), or any OAuth 2.0 provider (upstream()). Clients present a client ID metadata document or register (DCR), approve a server-owned consent page that names the server by its host, and receive the proxy's own opaque tokens (#2822)

New (server): the clients option limits which clients may connect, by metadata document URL, origin, or a client defined on the server (#2822)

New (server): the upstream client secret and user tokens stay on the server, encrypted in a shared store from mcp-use/oauth/storage: Upstash, Redis, Postgres, Firestore, Cloudflare D1 or Durable Object, or in-memory for local development. redisStorage takes a connected client or a lazy connect function (#2822)

New (server): tools read the upstream token with upstreamToken(ctx.auth) or ctx.auth.upstream (#2822)

Enhancement (server): failed sign-ins and refreshes log the cause without token or code values (provider error code and description, HTTP status and content type, mismatched iss, or network error); refused client metadata documents and records encrypted with a retired secret are also logged (#2822)

Enhancement (server): clients that signed in through the 1.x oauthProxy keep working while registration is on; users approve the consent page once and sign in again without removing the server (#2822)

New (server): OAuth providers can register public HTTP routes from setup() with host.route(), read host.mode and host.listenHost, and compute oauthMetadata from the resolved resource URL (#2822)

Fix (server): OAuth endpoints under the MCP path are never written to trace logs, and oauthEnvironmentValue no longer throws on runtimes without process (#2822)

Fix (server): trailing-slash trimming in upstashStorage and the GitHub and Google upstream providers no longer uses a backtracking regex

New (server, @mcp-use/cli): mcp-use build evaluates the entry with MCP_USE_PHASE=build and no longer needs runtime secrets; the new isBuilding() export lets module-scope code skip reading secrets or connecting to a database. oauthProxy and upstashStorage require no secrets or credentials while building (#2830)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use build exits when the build finishes, even if the entry opened a connection at module scope such as a Redis client (#2830)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use build builds for production when NODE_ENV is unset. Views no longer ship React's development build, and server-side JSX no longer compiles to jsxDEV, which failed under mcp-use start (#2830)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): a failed build or dev start prints the cause of a refused connection instead of an empty line (#2830)

New (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use deploy --no-github applies .gitignore rules when packaging, including wildcards, directory rules, and negation, while keeping the baseline cloud exclusions (#2485)

Fix (server): MCPServer.fromOpenAPI converts OpenAPI 3.0 boolean exclusiveMinimum and exclusiveMaximum into JSON Schema numeric bounds instead of throwing while registering tools (#2717)

Fix (@mcp-use/agent): the Anthropic provider sends "[no content]" for empty tool result content, avoiding HTTP 400 errors from the Messages API (#2693)

Documentation: add the OAuth Proxy guide, OAuth Proxy storage, v1 migration notes, and API reference; add GitHub and Google oauthProxy examples with Firestore (#2841, #2831)

Documentation: correct API reference comments: stdio env does not inherit the parent environment, defaultRequestOptions applies only to the initial tool listing, VMExecutorOptions.memoryLimitMb is not enforced, legacy stateless GET, DELETE, and HEAD return 204, and mcp-use/vite, mcp-use/tanstack-start, and mcp-use/tanstack-start/vite appear in the generated reference (#2838)

Update: patch vulnerable transitive dependencies (proxy-addr, shell-quote, source-map-js) and update Next.js examples to next ^16.3.8 (#2842)

items.title: October 14, 2026
items.text:
Summary

Agent Armor can now hold mail. In Hold mode, your agents hear about a message only once its scan finishes, and a message marked review stays held from them until someone releases it.

What's new?

Hold mode: an organization admin switches Agent Armor between Monitor, the default, and Hold in the console under Settings, then Labs. Hold sends no message.security.completed: the result arrives on message.received, or on message.security.review for a held message.

agent-armor-held label: a held message carries it until it is released, and its thread while any of its messages is held. List them by it, with include_spam, include_blocked and include_unauthenticated, to see held mail.

message.security.review: a webhook and WebSocket event sent when a message is held.

Release:POST /v0/inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/{message_id}/agent-armor/release releases a held message with a reason. Its message.received then goes to your agents, and message.security.override is sent too, in either order. Admins can also release from the console.

agent_armor_release permission: opt-in, so an agent's own key can't release mail held from it. See Permissions.

manual_override: a released message's agent_armor result records how, when and why it was released.

Use cases

Keep mail that may manipulate an agent away from it until a person has checked it.

Give a review tool, not your agents, the key that releases held mail.

items.text:
v4.1.0: Fourth and One

FastMCP 4.1.0 is a maintenance release at heart: a broad sweep of fixes across OpenAPI, proxies, auth, tasks, and the CLI, plus full Python 3.15 support. It doesn't change how most servers behave. A few security fixes do tighten inputs that FastMCP previously accepted, though, and our versioning policy keeps breaking changes out of patch releases, so this ships as a point-one release.

Check these before upgrading:

MultiAuth now qualifies client IDs by source, so existing MultiAuth sessions and tasks start new ownership scopes. Finish pending tasks before upgrading.

Regex tool search uses Pydantic's regex engine, which doesn't support lookarounds or backreferences.

Skill files must resolve inside their configured directories.

OpenAPI path parameters reject . and .. segments.

HTTP sessions now expire after the MCP SDK's 30-minute idle default instead of never.

CodeMode requires Monty 1.1, which renames max_duration_secs to max_feed_duration_secs.

Thanks to our 48 contributors, including 21 first-time contributors!

items.title: October 8, 2026
items.text:
Summary

Calendar is now in AgentMail Labs, so your organization can turn it on itself instead of asking us for beta access. An organization admin joins Labs once in the console, and every inbox's calendar becomes available to your agents right away.

What's new?

AgentMail Labs: a new Labs tab in the console's organization settings. An organization owner or admin joins (or leaves) Labs for the whole organization. Other members see the setting read-only.

Calendar in Labs: joining Labs turns on the calendar API for every inbox. API keys see the change within five minutes; the console shows it immediately.

Leaving Labs: calendar events are kept, but the calendar API returns 403, new invitations are not added, and event start and end webhooks stop until you rejoin.

Availability: Labs is available in US production (api.agentmail.to), not yet in EU production (api.agentmail.eu).

Organizations that were in the calendar beta were moved into Labs, so nothing changes for them.

Use cases

Give your agents a calendar the moment you need one, without waiting on a support request.

Try new AgentMail features early, for the whole organization, from one setting.

items.title: October 7, 2026
items.text:
Summary

Invitations are easier to keep up with. Every event the inbox can respond to now says how the inbox has answered, so an agent can find the invitations still waiting for a reply from the agenda alone. And an invitation email now records the calendar event it was applied to, so an agent can go from a message.received email straight to its event.

What's new?

response_status on calendar events: the status of the inbox's own entry in attendees, on the events Respond to Event accepts (email events from an organizer that list the inbox). It is on agenda and instance list items too, which leave out attendees, and in calendar webhook and WebSocket events. A date of a recurring invitation answered on its own reports that date's response. Events the inbox organizes have no response_status.

calendar_event_id on messages: set on an email once its calendar invitation, update, cancellation or attendee reply has been applied to the inbox's calendar, a few seconds after the email arrives. For an email about one date of a recurring event, it is that date's event ID. Pass it to Get Event. It is returned wherever a message is: Get Message, List Messages and Get Thread. Emails whose invitation was not imported have none.

SDKs: Python 2.0.14 and TypeScript 0.5.42 include both fields (response_status and calendar_event_id in Python, responseStatus and calendarEventId in TypeScript).

Use cases

Build agents that:

Answer every invitation still waiting for a reply, without getting each event

Handle an invitation email by looking at its event: check for conflicts, accept or decline, add notes in metadata

ChatGPT Plugin Extensions

Minor release adding typed ChatGPT Plugin Extensions across server and React APIs, with updated MCP SDKs and richer examples.

New (server): register typed global, thread, and file entrypoints on tool.view; launch contracts are validated and OpenAI tool metadata is preserved (#2737)

New (server): register native ChatGPT plugin settings with typed fields, optional layout, validated read/update tools, request context callbacks, and per-request capability advertisement. Applications keep control of persistence and authorization (#2739)

New (@mcp-use/react): useDeepLink reads the initial and subsequent ChatGPT deep-link URLs through the existing MCP App connection (#2738)

items.title: Desktop app improvements, agent comment replies, and more
items.text:
Desktop app

Deep links: mintlify:// links open in the desktop app as a new tab.

Zoom and new tabs: Zoom in, zoom out, or reset the zoom from the View menu. Cmd + N opens a new tab with a blank page.

Offline screen: Navigation changes you made while offline save when your connection returns. The app shows an offline screen if you lose your connection.

Find in page: Press Cmd + F to search the current page. See Keyboard shortcuts for more information.

Check for updates: Check for a new version from the app menu or settings. See Updates for more information.

Browser sign-in: Sign in to the desktop app through your default browser. If browser sign-in isn't available for your organization, sign in inside the app. See Sign in for more information.

Agent and AI

Agent replies to comments: The agent can read open comments and suggestions on a page, reply to threads, and resolve comment threads.

Google Docs integration: Connect Google Docs as a read-only personal integration so the agent can search and read your documents. Available on Enterprise plans.

Admin MCP: The admin MCP can edit your deploy branch directly when the branch doesn't require pull requests. It can also upload images and returns links to private pages. The diff shows who made each pending change.

Group-scoped MCP credentials: Assign user groups to MCP client credentials so they can access pages restricted to those groups. You can't change a credential's groups after you create it.

Custom skills on authenticated sites: Skills marked public: true appear for visitors who aren't signed in. See Share skills on authenticated sites.

Multiple pull requests per automation run: Custom automations can open several pull requests in one run, or add commits to a pull request that an earlier run opened. See Open multiple pull requests or append to open ones.

Editor and dashboard

Images in the editor: Click an image to select it. Drag it to move it, even inside frames, cards, tabs, and callouts, and resize it with handles that also work on touch screens. Dropped and pasted media lands between blocks.

Emoji reactions on text: Highlight text and react to it with an emoji. See Comments.

Publish warnings: The Publish menu warns you about open comments and labels unlisted pages as hidden.

Fewer confirmations: Source mode asks you to confirm a large change only when it exceeds 10,000 characters.

Keyboard shortcuts in the editor: Open Keyboard shortcuts from the dashboard help menu to see every shortcut. See View shortcuts in the dashboard for more information.

Starting page: Choose which dashboard page opens first. See Starting page for more information.

Preview access: Switch an existing preview between dashboard login and password protection. When you turn on authentication, choose whether to keep existing previews, delete public previews, or delete all previews. See Restrict access to preview deployments for more information.

Published sites and deployments

Page modes in every theme: Every theme supports center and frame page modes. In Maple and Almond, center mode keeps the sidebar and centers the content beside it. See Page mode for more information.

Endpoint frontmatter validation: Deployments fail if a page's api, openapi, or asyncapi frontmatter is a list instead of a single endpoint string, such as "GET /users".

Bug fixes

Editor: Ordered lists keep their numbering when you delete an empty middle item. Any block now renders between accordions in an AccordionGroup. Images pasted from other sites stay on the page. Source mode parses MDX import and export blocks correctly.

Private pages: Moving a private page to your site keeps its page ID and comments. Private pages load regardless of Git branch state.

Published sites: Images in table cells are zoomable. API playground requests without a body no longer send a Content-Type header. Search breadcrumbs match the page language. Willow renders custom page mode.

Assistant: The assistant widget on sites without authentication searches every page, not only pages marked public: true.

Authenticated sites: Generated OG images and PDF exports work on sites with authentication.

Previews: GitLab multi-repo preview deployments work, failed merge request comments no longer fail preview builds, and retargeting a pull request to your deploy branch creates a preview.

Agent: The editor agent uses your timezone.

Analytics: CSV exports escape spreadsheet formulas.

CLI: The CLI accepts AsyncAPI 3.0.0 specs on fresh installs.

items.title: Desktop app, page narration, webhook-triggered automations, and more
items.text:
Desktop app

Desktop app (beta): Use your dashboard and editor in a native app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Work in multiple tabs and windows, each with its own session. See Desktop app for more information and to download the app.

Editor

MDX checks in source mode: Source mode flags misspelled components, unknown or duplicate props, invalid prop values, missing required props, and unclosed tags. Hover over a flagged problem to apply a quick fix.

Autocomplete and hover definitions in source mode: Type < to get suggestions for components, props, and values, including page links, image paths, and icons. Hover over a component or prop to see its definition. See Visual and source mode.

Formatting in suggesting mode: In suggesting mode, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, and inline code changes become suggestions that teammates can accept or reject. See Suggestions.

Granular publishing: The Selective publishing setting is now called Granular publishing. By default, the Publish menu shows and publishes only your own changes. Turn on granular publishing to also choose from changes your teammates made. See Granular publishing.

List and table shortcuts: Cmd + Shift + 7 creates a numbered list and Cmd + Shift + 9 creates a task list. Use Ctrl instead of Cmd on Windows and Linux. Type [] and a space to start a task list. Tab and Shift + Tab indent and outdent every selected list item. In tables, Tab moves to the next cell and adds a row from the last cell. See Keyboard shortcuts.

Copy and paste: Copying keeps the structure, numbering, and formatting of lists. Pasting from Google Docs keeps bold text and links in lists, and Google Docs checklists and GitHub task lists paste as task lists.

Comments: Unsent comment drafts survive page reloads, replies stay put when a thread collapses, and a comment can contain only a mention. See Comments.

Private page roles: The Publisher role for sharing private pages is now called Full Access. Permissions are unchanged. See Share a private page.

Files: The Hidden files section is now called Files and lists every file in your repository that isn't in your navigation. See Files.

Faster editor: Pages open faster, typing no longer reparses the whole page, and navigation loads without waiting on GitHub data. When you switch projects, the editor reopens the page you last had open.

Agent and assistant

Image reading: The editor agent can view JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP images on your pages to describe them, write alt text, or check screenshots against the surrounding content. The assistant can also inspect images on the pages it reads. See View images.

Agent panel: The editor agent panel has a new design, is faster in long chats, folds long messages, and lets you start typing from anywhere in the panel.

Links to new pages: When the agent creates pages, its final message links to each one.

Assistant exports: Assistant CSV exports list the sources each answer cited.

Automations

Webhook triggers: Start a custom automation with an authenticated POST request to its webhook URL, using an organization API key with write access. Each request runs the automation's saved prompt. See Trigger a webhook automation.

Multiple pull requests per run: A custom automation can open several pull requests in one run. When its prompt asks, it can also add changes to open pull requests from its earlier runs.

Managing automations: Editors can now delete automations and triggers link to their repositories and channels.

Published sites

Narration (beta): Readers can listen to a page from a Listen to this page player at the top of the page. Mintlify highlights each sentence as it plays and skips code blocks, tables, and other non-prose content. Turn on narration in your project settings. Each generation uses 50 credits. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans. See Narration.

WebMCP: Mintlify registers your site's MCP tools in the browser, so browsers and in-browser agents that support WebMCP can search and read your docs while someone visits your site. No setup required. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans. See WebMCP.

Folder-level metatags: Set metatags for every page in a folder with seo.paths in docs.json. Page frontmatter now overrides metatags set in docs.json. See SEO settings.

MCP on authenticated sites: Hosted MCP servers no longer return 403 errors on sites with authentication enabled, and MCP settings appear for every project that uses authentication. See Enable authenticated MCP.

Dashboard and deployments

Projects: The dashboard now calls your deployments Projects instead of Sites.

Workspace name: Change your workspace name in your organization settings. Your organization's slug stays the same.

Rollbacks for editors: Editors can now roll back a deployment, not just admins. Available on Enterprise plans.

Faster multi-repo updates: Deployments with multiple repositories rebuild only what changed instead of running a full update.

mint validate: The command no longer copies static files, so it uses less disk space in repositories with many images.

Bug fixes

items.title: Scoped automation triggers, editor agent integrations, and more
items.text:
Automations

Scoped GitHub triggers: Custom automations can now trigger on GitHub topics and filter to paths and specific authors.

GitHub topic search: When you configure a repository-topic trigger, Mintlify suggests topics from your organization's repositories so you can pick one without leaving the settings page.

Automatic merge conflict resolution: Automations now resolve merge conflicts on their own pull requests without needing you to open the PR first. See Resolve merge conflicts.

Automations menu: A new Automations menu in the dashboard topbar links to your automations, runs, and settings. Sidebar automation cards show a live count of runs that need review.

Runs tab improvements: The Runs tab now shows a preview deployment link and lets you open a run in the editor, view run details, or edit the automation's settings.

Editor agent

Connected integrations as tools: The agent can call your connected third-party apps while researching and editing. The agent can prompt you to connect a new integration when it needs one.

Roll back edits: Ask the agent to undo a change and it reverts the pages it edited in the current session.

Current page context: The agent now sees the page you have open and its unsaved edits, so requests like "fix this section" apply to what you are working on.

Editor collaboration

@mentions: Type @ in a page to mention a teammate. Mentioned teammates get a notification.

Profile picture uploads: Upload a profile picture from your account settings. It appears on comments, mentions, and collaborator avatars.

Workspace folder icons: Edit the icon on a workspace folder from its menu. Folder metadata is preserved when you move or rename it.

Emoji favicons: A new Emojis tab in the icon picker lets you set an emoji as a page icon, and emoji icons render as the editor tab favicon.

Reorder shared and starred pages: Drag pages in Shared with me and Starred to set the order you want. The order syncs across your devices.

Version history redesign: The version history panel has a refreshed layout that's easier to scan when comparing revisions.

Faster editor rendering: Visual mode renders, switches pages, and scrolls faster.

Dashboard

Rebuilt Activity page: The Activity page has a new layout and shows richer details.

SSO login route: A new login route detects SSO configuration for your email domain and sends you to the right identity provider. The SSO connection limit is raised to 25.

Assistant layout settings: Deployment settings include options for the assistant layout so you can control how the assistant appears on your published site.

Analytics

Sort and export improvements: Page ratings support sort order, feedback shows the page URL, and assistant analytics exports include feedback ratings.

Page filter polish: The page filter opens on the currently selected page, resets with the clear button, and shows All pages as the default label.

Page-scoped popular pages, referrals, and top agents: These analytics widgets accept a page filter so you can drill into a single page.

Published sites

Related pages on authenticated sites: Related pages now appear on sites protected by Mintlify authentication.

Copy assistant responses: Select text and copy full responses from the assistant.

Bug fixes

Editor publishing: Pending edits are saved before publishing, deleted page titles show in the publish panel, publish retries when the branch lock is held, GitHub same-path replaces succeed, GitLab create collisions no longer break publish, and rows the server keeps after publish are preserved.

Editor: Language switcher options are disabled for pages without a translation, new page paths update until the first commit, slash commands rank by relevance, frontmatter edits are preserved during Git sync, source-mode comments no longer show false conflicts, and the page title is preserved across navigation.

Automations: Folder selection and topic search work correctly in the create flow, automatic conflict resolution skips mandatory PR mode when needed, and the trigger options popover collapses cleanly.

OpenAPI and API playground: Reverse-proxy guides render for sites with a base path, schema validation errors stay on one line, and locally-ignored OpenAPI specs are marked stale on full updates.

Client and hosting: RSS URLs no longer duplicate base paths, custom and frame pages render without a layout shift on load, and color swatches pick their theme value in CSS.

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.23 — Reasoning content and tool‑calling reliability
items.text: For gpt‑oss on POST /v1/chat/completions , reasoning content moves out of message.content and into choices.message.reasoning (non‑streaming) and choices.delta.reasoning (streaming), aligning with o3‑mini ‡ . Tool names are normalized (e.g., snake_case) before being provided to the model to improve tool‑calling reliability ‡ . Fixed errors for certain tools‑containing requests to POST /v1/chat/completions (e.g., "reading 'properties'") and non‑streaming tool‑call failures ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.19 — Bug fixes for streaming and tool calls
items.text: Corrected usage statistics returned by OpenAI‑compatible streaming responses ‡ . Improved handling of parallel tool calls via the streaming API ‡ . Fixed parsing of correct tool calls for certain Mistral models ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.18 — Streaming options and tool‑calling improvements
items.text: Added support for the stream_options object on OpenAI‑compatible endpoints. Setting stream_options.include_usage to true returns prompt and completion token usage during streaming ‡ . Errors returned from streaming endpoints now follow the correct format expected by OpenAI clients ‡ . Tool‑calling support added for Mistral v13 tokenizer models, using proper chat templates ‡ . The response_format.type field now accepts "text" in chat‑completion requests ‡ . Fixed bugs where parallel tool calls split across multiple chunks were dropped and where root‑level $defs in tool definitions were stripped ‡ .
